The arrival of Robo-taxi will engender many financial and social benefits for lower income individuals.


Consider the fact that many low income citizens lack personal transport and must rely on public transport and will often require a long walk to their final destination.

It will also allow people not only the ability to go to workplaces that were not available to them in the past, it also allow for easy access shopping, doctor's appointments and other necessary functions.


A side effect of robotaxi could result in a reduction of poverty, not a bad outcome.

comments.author: @Unoptimized
comments.text:
Musk says AI will surpass human intelligence next year, but I think this is the wrong way to think about AI. AI is just an increase in human language recursion. There's no reason to assume that it is somehow becoming like us. 

The first time humans were able to "externalize" language to a medium allowed us to exceed the human memory cap. This might have been a lithic symbol, or a painting of a deer, but that didn't mean that the rock or painting surpassed human intelligence or had better memory. That would be a very confused understanding of language. 

AI is also not unique in its ability to "run away" from us: iron tech, gunpowder, and nuclear fission have the same capacity. We are not relying on AI to reign AI in: we are relying on human language for this. Ultimately human language is paramount. Our capacity to offload to AI will make this easier than I think we're anticipating. Perhaps there will be a Catastrophe as in the transition from Bronze to Iron, but I think this might be avoided by putting teachable AI into everyone's pockets, rather than in the hands of a few men (even if they believe they're heroes). It requires a new model, but that's impossible given what is the current theory of language. 

Language is the only "recursive" function that modern science perceives in humans. But human violence is equally recursive (and therefore not at all like animal combat), and yet AI is prevented from being trained on violence. The Paradox is that violence is more universal and simpler, so the recursive property would be far more easily derived from it than *all language ever*. There's no way AI will understand recursion because it doesn't understand violence and has no language theory. So it's mechanations will eventually be relegated to elites only. 

The problem that Musk and other AI leaders are ignoring is that AI is only allowed to train on language data, and yet there's no coherent theory on language. Most mainstream language theories posits some external ecological factor that pushed some update to the genome that made us go from grunts to words, but this is extremely vague. A more coherent theory would posit that the human condition itself must produce language. Recursive, object based aggression (ROBA), which is unique to humans and exists in all human relations, renders language a necessity so that violence doesn't take over. This issue doesn't exist in animals, so their signals are shallow as a result. 

The current AI models only analyze the output of language. It's like telling AI to build a car by  giving it a lot of car exhaust and tire track data. It'll make something resembling a car but it will probably crash into a lot of things. It's sort of the same approach taken by Chomsky's Universal Grammar. Fascinating science, but you should talk to a mechanic first.

I'll release my ROBA Hypothesis white paper in the next couple weeks. It makes a more detailed argument. I'll also be presenting at COVR this summer in Mexico City, and I plan to present at the Generative Anthropology conference in Japan this summer as well. 

(This is an alternate account, in my day job I'm an action designer and stuntman, which is how I came upon this hypothesis - Eric Jacobus)
